ribbon.mark_prev_day: published the previous day at origin

reason.date_only: feed carries no time of day
reason.not_today: does not land on this date

filter.hint: Esc closes · c clears · OR within a row, AND across rows
filter.fx_caveat: unclassified means no rule matched, never "not FX"
filter.empty_ticker: no watchlisted ticker has items in this window
filter.empty_type: no source in this window has more than one type

watchlist.after_change: {message}. Filings appear after the next fetch.

tape.no_match_body: Filters combine as OR within a row and AND across rows, so narrowing two axes at once can leave nothing.
tape.empty_body: No filters are active — the last 30 days are genuinely empty.
tape.no_sources_body: Every source in sources.yaml has enabled: false, so nothing is being collected. Set enabled: true on the ones you want, then run a fetch.

rail._note_source_facts: !! DO NOT PUT A PUBLICATION TIME IN THESE. The {time}, {day} and {release} placeholders are filled with facts about the PUBLISHER - '4pm AEST', '09:15 CST', '~16:00 CET', 'Fri 15:30 ET' - and those are true for every reader in every timezone. Translate the words around them. Writing '4pm 澳东标准时间 · {period}' here looks like doing the job and silently breaks a source fact. A test fails if any of those strings appears in a locale file.
rail.cot_asof: CFTC non-commercial net, contracts · as of {period} ({day}), released {release}
rail.health_unreachable_many: {n} of {total} sources are unreachable. When it is most of them, the connection is the more likely cause than the sources.

risk.rest_refetchable: Everything else is re-fetchable: losing it costs polling time, not data.
risk.export_never: not exported yet — run {command}, or set {setting} in sources.yaml to a synced folder and it happens automatically.
risk.export_protected: Exporting to {path} — {n} row(s) protected {when}. Off this disk, so a drive failure costs nothing.
risk.export_stale: Exporting to {path}, but the file is out of date — run {fetch} or {export}.
risk.export_local: {n} row(s) exported to {path}{stale} — that is the same disk as the database, so it protects against a mistake but not a drive failure. Set {setting} in sources.yaml to a synced folder.

never_polled.label: not polled yet
never_polled.meaning: This source has never been fetched. Nothing is wrong.
never_polled.action: Run `python -m macrowire fetch` to collect from it.

healthy.label: polled
healthy.meaning: Last poll succeeded and stored what it found.

no_change.label: polled, nothing new
no_change.meaning: The source was contacted and reported nothing new. A successful poll - this is the normal outcome for a source that publishes once a day.

throttled.label: within interval
throttled.meaning: The rate limiter blocked this cycle before any request went out, to stay inside the source's polite interval.

log_incomplete.label: data current, log incomplete
log_incomplete.meaning: This source holds data newer than any fetch it has logged - usually a restore from a backup taken before that fetch. The data is fine; only the log is missing.
log_incomplete.action: Harmless. The next successful fetch clears it.

failing.label: failing
failing.meaning: Consecutive failures since the last good cycle.
failing.action: Check the error kind: `network` is usually transient, `http_404` suggests the feed has moved or been withdrawn.

stale.label: stale
stale.meaning: Polling works, but the source has published nothing new for longer than its configured threshold.
stale.action: Usually the source being quiet. Confirm on its website before assuming a fault.

unreachable.label: network unreachable
unreachable.meaning: Every attempt since the last good cycle timed out or never connected. Nothing came back, so this says nothing about the source - it may be connectivity rather than the source.
unreachable.action: If other sources are reaching their servers, this one's route is the difference. Raise timeout_seconds for it in sources.yaml if the link is slow, or set enabled: false to stop polling it.
unreachable.short: network unreachable — may be connectivity rather than the source

disabled.label: disabled
disabled.meaning: enabled: false in sources.yaml. This source is not contacted at all. Anything already collected from it is kept and still shows on the tape.
disabled.action: Set enabled: true in sources.yaml to start polling it.

fetch.disabled_detail: enabled: false in sources.yaml; not contacted
fetch.none_enabled: Every source in sources.yaml has enabled: false, so this cycle contacted nothing. Set enabled: true on the ones you want polled.
fetch.some_disabled: {n} of {total} sources are disabled and were not contacted.

first_run.gitignored: That directory is gitignored: cloning this repo gives you the code, not the data. Every install builds its own history by polling.
first_run.outside: That is outside the project directory, so it is not affected by anything the repository does. Every install builds its own history.
first_run.refetchable: Most of what accumulates is re-fetchable - SEC, NBS, CFETS, ECB and the news feeds all serve their recent history on request, so losing the database costs polling time rather than data.
first_run.irreplaceable: The exception is {sources}: those feeds carry one item and no archive, so what you collect is the only copy in existence.
first_run.export_hint: Set export.path in sources.yaml to a synced folder and your irreplaceable rows are backed up automatically.

status.contacted_nothing_new: (contacted; nothing new, so no store logged)
status.log_incomplete: DATA CURRENT, LOG INCOMPLETE — stored {when}, newer than any logged contact. A restore from a backup predating that fetch is the usual cause.
status.risk_no: our copy is the only one
status.risk_partial: only the live window is re-fetchable
status.fx_drift: DRIFT: {recent}% unclassified in the last 30d vs {older}% before - the source may have renamed something the vocabulary matches on.
status.unreachable: network unreachable - may be connectivity rather than the source. Every attempt since the last good cycle timed out or never connected, so nothing has come back to judge the source by.
status.unreachable_hint: Raise timeout_seconds for this source if the link is slow, or set enabled: false to stop polling it.

watchlist.empty_hint: add one with:  python -m macrowire watchlist add AAPL
watchlist.empty_note: Company filings poll nothing until you do.
watchlist.empty_markets_cn: US tickers are collected via SEC EDGAR and mainland China codes (six digits) via CNINFO, the CSRC-designated disclosure portal covering both Shanghai and Shenzhen. Both are validated on add. Other markets can be recorded with --market but nothing polls them yet: ASX and HKEX both prohibit automated access, so neither is a source.

serve.running: MacroWire on http://{host}:{port}  ({host} only, no auth)
serve.stop_it: stop it with:  python -m macrowire stop --port {port}
serve.not_ours: that is not a macrowire server - stop it yourself, or use --port for a one-off.
serve.uninspectable: held by a process this user cannot inspect.
serve.closing: nothing is listening on it - the socket is probably still closing from a previous run. Try again in a moment.
serve.stop_uninspectable: port {port} is held by a process this user cannot inspect
serve.stop_not_ours: pid {pid} on port {port} is not a macrowire server; refusing to kill it
serve.stop_survived: pid {pid} still holds port {port} after SIGKILL

export.external: written outside the project to {path} - a drive failure costs nothing
export.local: written to {path}, the same disk as the database.
export.local_hint: Set export.path in sources.yaml to a synced folder and these rows are backed up automatically.
export.repo_hint: (this directory is a git repo, so committing the file is one way to get it off the disk)

backup.same_disk: same disk as the database - protects against a mistake, not a drive failure.
backup.move_hint: Set backup.path in sources.yaml to move them off it.

errors.sec_contact: SEC_CONTACT is not set. The SEC requires a User-Agent of the form 'Name email' and enforces it with a 403.

backfill.done: {requests} request(s) made, {stored} observation(s) stored, {skipped} page(s) already had.
backfill.no_history: {source} has no backfill_start, backfill_url or backfill_page_size in sources.yaml - this source has no retrievable history
backfill.kept: Everything fetched before that point is stored; resuming re-asks only what is left.
backfill.debug_hint: Full traceback: re-run with --debug, or see fetch_log.

restore.warning: the current database will be moved aside, not deleted.

help.backfill_dry: show the plan, make no requests

help.debug: show the full traceback instead of a summary

help.prefs_clear: remove one preference so sources.yaml applies

locales.orphaned_head: {locale} has {n} key(s) that do not exist in {default}:
locales.orphaned_note: A key with no English original cannot fall back, so it renders in one language only. Usually a typo or a string removed from en.
locales.partial_note: A partial locale is usable: every missing key falls back to {default} on its own, so nothing renders blank or as a raw key.
locales.contribute: To add one: copy {default}.json, translate the values, save it as <code>.json alongside, and set locale in sources.yaml. Translate values only - never the keys, and never a publication time.

prefs.note: Stored in the database, never written to sources.yaml. Set them in the interface, or clear one with: python -m macrowire prefs --clear <key>

settings.title: Settings
settings.viewer_note: Yours, stored per user. Changing these never edits sources.yaml.
settings.install_note: From {path}, shown read-only. Edit the file to change them.
settings.timezone_note: Where YOU are. A source's publication time never moves with it.
settings.reload_note: Language and timezone changes redraw the page.

coverage.recoverable_body: Coverage starts {date}. This source answers for older dates — {command} reaches further back.
coverage.unwired_body: Coverage starts {date}. This source has a queryable archive, but no backfill is configured for it in sources.yaml.
coverage.lost_body: Coverage starts {date}. This feed carries only its most recent entries; what scrolled off before the first fetch on {first} is gone and cannot be recovered.
coverage.never_body: Coverage starts {date} — the day collection began. This feed carries one item and no archive, so nothing before that date exists in any copy.
coverage.end_missing: Not in the record for this period:
coverage.end_complete: All {n} sources are complete for this window.
coverage.end_rest_complete: The other {n} are complete for this window.
